add.title: LGBT rights in Brazil (Wikipedia) - LGBTQ people in Brazilian prisons
add.summary: Wikipedia's 'LGBT rights in Brazil' (fetched and read in full, 4 Oct 2026) states, in its Politics section, that LGBTQ people have a special place in Brazilian prisons, separate from other prisoners; that transsexuals have the right to be called by their social name and not their birth name and to be forwarded to women's prisons; and that LGBTQ people in prisons may choose male or female clothing. The sentence is footnoted to G1's 17 Apr 2014 report ('Governo publica portaria com direitos para presos gays e travestis', archived 12 Jul 2018) - i.e., the cited legal grounding is a 2014 federal portaria granting rights to gay and travesti prisoners. Placement axis: on paper, placement follows gender identity (trans prisoners forwarded to women's prisons), with separate custody for LGBTQ prisoners, social-name use and clothing choice; the underlying citation is dated (2014) and its current status was not independently re-verified.

add.title: LGBTQ people in prison (Wikipedia) - Brazil section
add.summary: Wikipedia overview article (fetched and read in full, 4 Oct 2026). Its Transgender issues > Brazil section contains no trans-prisoner placement rule - only discussion of social vulnerability, stigma and fragmented identity of travestis and transgender people during rehabilitation; international sections show placement norms elsewhere (e.g., Canada placing by gender identity, Italy's admission discretion). Negative evidence: this general overview documents no Brazil-specific trans-prisoner housing policy, special unit or segregation-for-placement practice.
